children.text: Selected work across technology and healthcare, spanning AI hardware, software and consumer apps. Take a closer look at the projects, and how I approached their market research, growth strategy and go-to-market challenges.

children.name: Halali is a halal food delivery, pickup an
children.text:
Halali is a halal food delivery, pickup and discovery platform in Sydney. It connects customers with verified halal restaurants, helping them find food that meets their requirements with greater confidence.

As of October 2026, Halali has completed its angel funding round and is raising a pre-Series A round.

children.name: Trust was central to the product. Customer
children.text: Trust was central to the product. Customers with strict halal requirements needed confidence in how restaurants were verified, including Halali's policy of excluding mixed kitchens. At the same time, the platform needed a distinct position in a crowded delivery market alongside Uber Eats, DoorDash and other established apps. The challenge was to reach Muslim communities through both digital channels and local, on-the-ground activity, then turn awareness into sustained use.

children.name: I defined the North Star metric and develo
children.text: I defined the North Star metric and developed a growth framework covering acquisition, activation, referrals and ongoing engagement. This included a referral plan, creator partnerships and community outreach, with online promotion and local activation planned together. I also built a dashboard using AI-assisted coding to organise content planning and monitor growth metrics and operational data.

children.text: Built with AI-assisted coding to bring content planning, performance metrics and operational data into one view.

children.name: MuseKey is an AI-powered music instrument
children.text:
MuseKey is an AI-powered music instrument for children. It turns a hum, a tap or a recorded sound into an original song that children can save, replay and share, making music creation part of everyday play.

As of October 2026, MuseKey has completed its angel funding round and is raising a pre-Series A round.

children.name: International Market Research & Early Go-t
children.text:
International Market Research & Early Go-to-Market

I researched potential audiences, demand, competing alternatives and international markets to inform the product's early positioning and launch direction.

children.name: MuseKey had no clear benchmark or establis
children.text: MuseKey had no clear benchmark or established go-to-market playbook. The first questions were whether families would pay for it and which families were most likely to do so. Research needed to explore household income, views on children's education, familiarity with AI, understanding of the product and priorities for its hardware and software. The team also needed to understand the child-related and AI-related regulatory considerations in potential markets.

children.name: I used AI research tools to examine social
children.text: I used AI research tools to examine social media discussions, Reddit threads and Amazon reviews of related technology and educational products, looking at both positive and negative experiences. I conducted quantitative research using Prolific and Qualtrics to explore pain points, willingness to pay, price expectations and feature priorities. I also carried out qualitative research and follow-up with five families, bringing these findings together to inform positioning and early go-to-market recommendations.

children.text:

children.text:
Go-to-Market Research & Strategy

I translated an open-ended international launch brief into market research and an initial go-to-market strategy, delivered through a browsable HTML report.

children.name: The product had a working demo, but its in
children.text: The product had a working demo, but its international launch direction was unclear. Which skiers needed it most? Which markets should come first? Where could it stand apart from competitors, and how could the team reach early users? My task was to turn these questions into evidence-based market priorities and a practical starting point for launch planning.

children.name: I defined the research brief around target
children.text:
I defined the research brief around target users, market priorities, competitors and acquisition channels. I reviewed competitor websites, features and positioning to build a comparison matrix, then analysed App Store reviews and Reddit discussions for user pain points and language. I kept sources traceable and separated findings from interpretations and assumptions that still needed testing.

I proposed a role for each early channel: Reddit for understanding needs and recruiting testers; TikTok for technique demonstrations and before-and-after comparisons; Instagram for building credibility and trust; Product Hunt for launch feedback; and a landing page to explain the product and capture interest. The HTML report brought these recommendations together with the market priorities, competitor matrix and user insights to support the team's launch decisions.
